title: Cellular Respiration
seo_title: Grade 7 Cellular Respiration Worksheets: Glucose, Oxygen, Mitochondria and Energy
standard_text: Develop a model to describe how food is rearranged through chemical reactions forming new molecules that support growth and/or release energy as this matter moves through an organism.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on cellular respiration (NGSS MS-LS1-7): glucose and oxygen to carbon dioxide, water and energy, mitochondria, comparing photosynthesis, and yeast experiments. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_sub: In mitochondria, glucose and oxygen react to form carbon dioxide and water, releasing energy for life.
body_html:
How to think about it

Living things get energy from food through cellular respiration, which happens in the mitochondria of plant and animal cells:

glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water + energy

First, digestion breaks food into small molecules such as glucose. Blood carries glucose and oxygen to cells. In cells, chemical reactions rearrange the atoms: some molecules are broken down to release energy, and some are rebuilt into new molecules for growth and repair.

Respiration is the reverse of photosynthesis, so the two processes cycle carbon and oxygen.

Example

What gas fills a balloon on a bottle of yeast and sugar?

Yeast does respiration.

CO₂ is a product.

Answer: carbon dioxide

Example

Do plant cells do respiration?

All living cells need energy.

Answer: Yes.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking respiration just means breathing.
  • Thinking only animals do respiration.
  • Thinking food turns directly into energy without chemical reactions.

faq.a: A chemical process in cells that uses glucose and oxygen to release energy, producing carbon dioxide and water.

faq.q: How is cellular respiration related to photosynthesis?
faq.a: They are opposite processes. Photosynthesis makes glucose and oxygen; respiration uses them and releases carbon dioxide and water.
Yes. Plant cells break down the sugar they make to get energy, just like animal cells.
